articles.headline: Chase's fiery halftime speech inspires Bengals to comeback win vs. Ravens
articles.description: Ja'Marr Chase unloaded on his Bengals teammates in a halftime speech that inspired Cincinnati to a comeback victory over the Ravens.
articles.headlineJa: チェイスの熱いハーフタイムスピーチがベンガルズを鼓舞、レイブンズ相手に逆転勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ジャマール・チェイスがハーフタイムにチームメイトへ激しい叱咤激励を浴びせたことが、シンシナティがレイブンズ相手に逆転勝利を収める原動力となった。
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- Ja'Marr Chase was fuming about what he saw from his team in the first half of Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.

So when the team entered the locker room at halftime, the Cincinnati Bengals star wide receiver made sure he let his teammates know how he felt. The All-Pro unloaded in a halftime speech that let the offense know that things needed to be better.

Message received.

The Bengals scored five unanswered touchdowns in a 35-13 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. All of those points came in the second half following Chase's bold words.

"I came in here screaming, saying, 'Somebody's got to make a play for us, somebody got to make a play,'" Chase said. "And I told our offense [that] we can't look at our defense the whole time. We've got to step this s--- up and make something work."

Heading into Sunday, Cincinnati (4-2) had lost three straight games in AFC North play and dropped six of the past eight regular-season contests against the Ravens (3-3). And even though Baltimore was without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, it dominated the first half.

The Ravens outgained Cincinnati 258 yards to 59 in the first half and had 20 more offensive plays than the Bengals. That was the lowest yardage in any first half in any game featuring quarterback Joe Burrow, whom Cincinnati drafted with the first overall pick in 2020, according to ESPN Research. The performance set Chase off.

"I didn't like how we played," Chase said. "We had [19] plays, maybe two or three possessions. And it didn't go our way at all. We had opportunities to get the ball out of our hands, and Joe was getting too much pressure."

But the second-half adjustments worked. Cincinnati, which gave up eight third-down possessions in the first half, buckled down after the break. Not only did the offense find a rhythm that was missing at the start of the game, but the defense opened the half with a three-and-out and a turnover on downs deep in Bengals territory.

Even though Chase's message was aimed at the offense, the players on the other side of the ball took heed of what was said.

"That's a guy who loves to compete at the highest level -- he wants to win," said linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr., who had an interception in the win. "I believe once you hear a guy like that, who's a leader on this team, speak up on the offense side of the ball, that just encourages you."

Knight said it was a reset for the entire team. And the result was one of the more dramatic scoreboard flips in NFL history.

Baltimore became the third team ever to lead by 13 or more points at halftime and lose by 20 or more, according to ESPN Research. Initially, the Ravens looked poised for another blowout win after a 24-0 drubbing at Cincinnati in last year's final meeting between the two teams. Instead, Cincinnati produced a showing that indicated what its quality could be by the end of the season, coach Zac Taylor said.

articles.headline: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid player ratings as Kylian Mbappé sinks out-of-sorts hosts
articles.description: A brace from Kylian Mbappé -- the latter his 100th goal for the club -- claimed a famous victory for Real Madrid over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナ対レアル・マドリードの選手評：キリアン・エムバペが不調のホームチームを撃破
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペが2得点（クラブでの通算100ゴール目）を挙げ、レアル・マドリードはスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウでのバルセロナ戦で劇的な勝利を飾った。
articles.body:
A brace from Kylian Mbappé -- the latter his 100th goal for the club -- claimed a famous victory for Real Madrid over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou.

Having won every game so far in LaLiga, Barcelona looked extremely vulnerable to the Frenchman's pace in behind and eventually paid the price, letting Madrid back into the title race when they could, realistically, have been out of sight already.

Here, ESPN rates both sets of players after a dramatic Clásico.

Barcelona

Manager rating (out of 10)

Hansi Flick, 4 -- A rare off night for one of the best managers in the world. Barcelona have obviously had wonderful results playing a high line so far this season but Mbappé's pace allowed him to get in behind almost at will, and only poor service to the Frenchman prevented him getting even more chances.

Player ratings (1-10; 10 = best, 5 = average)

GK Joan García, 5 -- Couldn't have done much about either of the goals. Pulled off a couple of smart saves, most notably to deny Arda Güler.

RB Xaxi Espart, 5 -- Showed a couple of neat touches but withdrawn with an injury on the half-hour mark.

CB Pau Cubarsí, 4 -- Not his usual assured self. Struggled with Mbappé's pace in behind as Barcelona played a very high line. Needed Gerard Martín to bail him out when he dived in on Bellingham on the halfway line, missed the ball and presented Madrid with a two-on-one. Also caught out for Mbappé's winner.

CB Gerard Martín, 6 -- Struggled in the first half, and made a poor mistake for the opening goal, even if it was a little unfortunate. But looked a different player in the second and snuffed out a glorious chance for Bellingham and Mbappé, positioning his body perfectly between them when he was left all alone to deal with their counter-attack. Could have scored, but for a brilliant Lunin save.

LB João Cancelo, 4 -- Looked less comfortable when moved to right back after Xavi Espart's injury. Could not keep up with Yan Diomande's blistering speed.

DM Rodri, 5 -- As the anchor in Barcelona's midfield, he may feel a little disappointed with how open Barcelona were in the 15-minute period either side of halftime. Showed some neat touches on the ball, especially as the hosts began to dominate in the closing stages.

DM Pedri, 6 -- Struggled to assert himself in the first half but pulled out a nice assist in the second and looked much-improved from then on. Was key to Barcelona keeping the pressure on in the closing stages.

RW Lamine Yamal, 6 -- Marc Cucurella looked to have been told by Mourinho to antagonise the young winger, and it certainly worked in the first half. Had the perfect chance to level the scoring almost instantly after Mbappé's opener but shanked his finish well wide. Improved in the second and had a number of decent efforts, but overall will be disappointed he could not take his sparkling form into this game.

AM Fermín López, 6 -- Classy footballer. Carried the ball well through midfield but struggled to impact the game in the final third.

articles.headline: Jeff Hafley, Dolphins hold off Jets, then revel in first win of season
articles.description: The Dolphins snapped a five-game losing streak to win their first game of the season, holding off a late New York Jets rally for a 28-25 victory.
articles.headlineJa: ジェフ・ハフリー率いるドルフィンズがジェッツを退け、今季初勝利を喜ぶ
articles.descriptionJa: ドルフィンズは、終盤のニューヨーク・ジェッツの猛追を28-25で凌ぎ、5連敗を止めて今シーズン初勝利を挙げた。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley grew up in Montvale, New Jersey, roughly 20 miles away from where his team played Sunday.

His coaching career was already well underway by the time MetLife Stadium opened in 2010, but he could still feel the nostalgia as he entered it Sunday morning.

"I have a lot of memories here, a lot of memories of my dad and thinking of me as a little kid in the parking lot as we came in," he said. "I mean, I was one of those guys flipping off the buses and now here I am. Somehow it worked out where now I'm coaching here."

After Sunday, he'll have another memory to add to his collection.

The Dolphins snapped a five-game losing streak to win their first game of the season, holding off a late New York Jets rally for a 28-25 victory. Coming off a Week 6 bye, the Dolphins never trailed and captured their first lead of the season on their opening drive.

Hafley appeared stoic as he walked into the locker room after the game but was met with explosive cheers as soon as he rounded the corner.

"I think [Hafley] was very excited -- it was probably pent-up excited, too," Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis said. "I feel like we could have won the last few games that we played. We've been in them competing, and we just got the result we wanted today. So guys can really be super proud of what they put in, all the work they put in."

Willis turned in what Hafley called his best game of the season, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, both to rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas.

The Dolphins took a 21-7 lead into halftime thanks to a 15-play, 91-yard drive at the end of the first half, during which Willis executed three critical scrambles. The first was a 5-yard run on fourth-and-2 to keep the drive alive. Seven plays later, he scored on a 2-yard bootleg with six seconds remaining in the half.

Between those two runs, Willis also scrambled for 7 yards on second-and-6, sliding in-bounds to keep the clock running.

After the game, Hafley credited his quarterback for his situational awareness.

"I think that [Willis' awareness is] growing," Hafley said. "So if you look at Malik and now the six games, the body of work -- it's like a sixth game as basically a rookie starter. So he's going to learn and we need to see him make those plays. That was actually right down in front of me, I saw him and it was good. He was decisive today. He was decisive and I thought he competed today at a really, really high level."

Dolphins players have insisted throughout the first month-plus of the season that they needed to learn how to win. But first, Hafley said, they needed to learn how to play with a lead.

The Jets cut their deficit to one score with an Omar Cooper Jr. touchdown midway through the third quarter and threatened to tie the game with first-and-goal from the Dolphins' 1 early in the fourth. articles.headline: 49ers 'took a step back' in first loss of season against Falcons
articles.description: On Sunday, after the Niners blew an 11-point lead and lost their first game of the season to the Atlanta Falcons, Warner had the distinct feeling that the outcome directly aligned with a lack of progress.
articles.headlineJa: 49ers、ファルコンズに今季初敗戦、「後退した」との声
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日、49ersが11点のリードを溶かしてアトランタ・ファルコンズに今季初戦を落とすと、ワーナーは、この結果がチームの停滞を直接的に反映しているという強い感覚を抱いた。
articles.body:
ATLANTA - After each of the San Francisco 49ers' six wins this season, linebacker Fred Warner insisted he isn't as worried about the final score as whether his team showed improvement from the previous week.

On Sunday, after the Niners blew an 11-point lead and lost their first game of the season to the Atlanta Falcons, Warner had the distinct feeling that the outcome directly aligned with a lack of progress.

"Unfortunately, we're not going undefeated this year," Warner said after the 29-20 defeat. "It's not just about winning. I've said we have to continue to get better as a team. I feel like today we didn't get better. We took a step back."

While the Falcons made their share of impressive plays, the Niners buoyed that upset bid with an avalanche of mistakes, many of which were self-inflicted. That included four turnovers, three of which were inside Atlanta's 30, with no takeaways, seven penalties for 55 yards -- four of those on the defense and all giving the Falcons a first down and three of those coming on third or fourth down.

What's more, the 49ers continued their special teams struggles with kicker Eddy Pineiro missing his fourth extra point of the season and the kick coverage unit allowing returns of 61 and 38 yards.

In an otherwise winnable game, the Niners did all they could to help the Falcons improve to 3-4 while losing for the first time in their past 19 tries when leading by 11 or more points.

"That was one of the most frustrating things," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Anytime you have four turnovers like that and you get zero, it's real tough to win.

"I don't know about the amount of penalties, but the timing of some penalties, just keeping them on the field, giving them some big plays, especially when we have them behind the chains, just illegal contacts or holdings, whatever they called. But too sloppy to win."

Early on, it looked like the Niners might cruise to their seventh consecutive victory and head into the bye as one of the league's lone undefeated teams. Despite missing almost all of their top receivers, including Mike Evans (Achilles), because of injury, they jumped to a 14-3 lead after impressive touchdown drives on two of their first three possessions.

Even after running back Christian McCaffrey departed with a thigh injury, rookie running back Kaelon Black rattled off three runs for 52 yards, including a 30-yard score. But with the 49ers marching to potentially take a 21-9 lead, Black fumbled at Atlanta's 29.

Soon after, defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa jumped offsides on a fourth-and-4 just before halftime when the Falcons clearly were trying to draw the penalty, allowing Atlanta to manage a field goal just before the end of the second quarter.

articles.headline: Vikings rally to reach 6-0 even as offense hits historic lows for unbeaten team
articles.description: As his offense continued to grind Sunday at historically low levels for an undefeated team, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell had a simple message: "We're not far off."
articles.headlineJa: バイキングス、攻撃陣が歴史的な低迷を見せるも6勝0敗を維持
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日の試合でも、無敗チームとしては歴史的な低水準の攻撃が続いたが、バイキングスのケビン・オコネル監督は「あと少しだ」とシンプルなメッセージを送った。
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- As his offense continued to grind Sunday at historically low levels for an undefeated team, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell had a simple message.

"We're not far off," O'Connell said after his team came from behind to defeat the Indianapolis Colts 16-10 to improve their record to 6-0. The Vikings have the best record in the NFC, largely because of the league's top defense and one of its best special teams, while the offense has scored the second-fewest points (125) by a 6-0 team since 1940. Their 10 touchdowns are the fewest by a team with their record since the 1933 Chicago Bears.

Time is running out, however, for the offense to catch up. After defeating four teams that currently have losing records among their first six opponents, the Vikings are about to face the most difficult segment of their schedule.

Their next four games are a gauntlet, coming against the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Green Bay Packers and San Francisco 49ers. Only the Bills game will be played at U.S. Bank Stadium.

"You can't get down on it right now," O'Connell said, "just because it's still relatively early enough that we're catching our stride. But at the same time, we know what type of people and teams that are going to be on our schedule the rest of the way, and where we want to go with this team."

The Vikings' key offensive players landed on a similar message of forced optimism.

"We'll continue to get better," quarterback Kyler Murray said. "I know we will. I know everybody keeps saying that, but I felt like we moved the ball well today."

Said receiver Justin Jefferson: "It's just only going to get more comfortable and more comfortable as the season goes on. It's just the bye week, getting a little rust out in the first half, and definitely things just moving a little bit better the second half."

In some ways, Sunday's game was a step back after the Vikings had put up a season-high 364 total yards in Week 5 during their 23-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints. Murray powered that surge with seven scrambles for 54 yards, and the offense was struggling in all phases Sunday until he took off on a 35-yard scramble to convert a third down on the final play of the third quarter. Prior to that run, the Vikings had managed only 128 offensive yards and two field goals from Will Reichard.

Murray threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end T.J. Hockenson on the first play of the fourth quarter to give the Vikings their first lead at 13-10.

Afterward, O'Connell rattled off a series of near-misses, including two incomplete passes Murray threw toward Jefferson -- one that was a step behind Jefferson and another that fell short because the pass rush prevented him from stepping into the throw. articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé scores 100th goal for Real Madrid in dramatic Clásico win
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has scored his 100th goal for Real Madrid.
articles.headlineJa: エムバペ、劇的なクラシコの勝利でレアルでの100ゴール目を達成
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペが、レアル・マドリードでの通算100ゴール目を記録した。
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé scored his 100th goal for Real Madrid to give his side a dramatic 2-1 Clásico win over Barcelona on Sunday. 

The record goal from Mbappé came in the 87th minute of the game to give Madrid a priceless lead after Eduardo Camavinga laid off to him in the box for the Frenchman to tuck home into an empty net.

It came after his first of the game, which was a rather fortuitous strike in the first half. A Gerard Martín attempted clearance was hit straight at Mbappé, who then finished past Joan García to give Madrid the lead. 

Raphinha had equalized for Barça in the second half, but Mbappé's late strike secured all three points for Madrid and put them just three points behind their rivals at the top of LaLiga. It also handed Barça their first league defeat of the season. 

Mbappé's match-winning brace comes a day before the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, an award for which the Madrid superstar is very much in the running.

Mbappé is the 24th player to reach a century of goals for Spain's most successful club and the fourth fastest to do so, joining the likes of Alfredo di Stéfano, Raúl and Cristiano Ronaldo, who sits top of the rankings with 450 goals in 438 matches.

Despite being LaLiga's top scorer in both of his full seasons at the club, Mbappé is yet to win any trophies with Madrid, having lost out on the LaLiga title to Barcelona in both 2024-25 and 2025-26.

- What it takes to win a Ballon d'Or: Trophies, goals and playing the PR game

- Barcelona's Yamal vs. Madrid's Mbappé: Which star has stronger Ballon d'Or claim?

- A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?

The Frenchman joined Madrid on a free transfer in June 2024 after scoring 256 goals in 308 appearances for Paris Saint-Germain and 27 in 60 for AS Monaco.

The 27-year-old also became France's all-time leading scorer, as well as the top scorer in World Cup history, this summer.

articles.headline: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard to miss Wolves game with knee swelling
articles.description: Raptors star Kawhi Leonard is out for Sunday night's game against the Timberwolves due to left knee swelling.
articles.headlineJa: ラプターズのカワイ・レナード、膝の腫れによりウルブズ戦を欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: ラプターズのスター、カワイ・レナードは、左膝の腫れのため日曜夜のティンバーウルブズ戦を欠場する。
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard will miss his first game this season due to what the Toronto Raptors are calling left knee swelling.

The All-NBA forward will miss Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

In his first season back with the Raptors since helping to win the franchise's first NBA championship in 2019, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in two games this season.

Leonard has an extensive history of right knee issues including an ACL tear in 2021 and a meniscus tear in 2023. The LA Clippers, who traded Leonard to Toronto before the season, load-managed Leonard for much of his tenure there due to issues with the knee.

articles.headline: Breaking down Cowboys-Eagles MNF matchup in wide-open NFC East
articles.description: Both teams enter the game 2-4, looking far from formidable and staring up at the 4-2-1 division-leading Giants.
articles.headlineJa: 混戦のNFC東地区、カウボーイズ対イーグルスのMNF対決を徹底分析
articles.descriptionJa: 両チームとも2勝4敗と、手強いとは言い難い状態で試合に臨んでおり、4勝2敗1分けで地区首位を走るジャイアンツを見上げる立場にある。
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark summed up the state of the NFC East pretty darn well last week. 

"We lost and we're seeing everybody else lose," he said. 

From Weeks 5 to 6, the NFC East is the first division in NFL history to go winless in consecutive weeks in which all teams in the division played a game, according to ESPN Research. The New York Giants (4-2-1) and Washington Commanders (1-4-1) came into the season without great expectations, but the Philadelphia Eagles and Cowboys were supposed to be the class of the division and Monday's game (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN/ABC) is a matchup of two potential NFC powers looking to get an early advantage in playoff positioning. 

Instead, both teams enter 2-4, looking far from formidable and staring up at the division-leading Giants. 

The Eagles can vouch for Murphy's Law. They've dealt with one blow after another, the most recent being the loss of franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts because of blood clots in his lungs. They've scored 24 points or fewer in nine straight games and are losers of four straight.

The Cowboys needed an uptick in defensive play this season to complement their high-flying offense. Instead, the defense has been about as giving as ever and the offense has gotten worse from a season ago. 

So, it's not how either team drew it up. But with every team scrambling, the NFC East crown is as gettable as ever. 

"You're not looking too far ahead, but the NFC East is struggling and the NFC East is really asking for someone to take it over," Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said. "It's going to be a team that figures it out and starts playing at a high level. We have the opportunity. We have that chance. Even with all these injuries and with all the crazy things that are happening, we have a lot of talent." 

ESPN's Eagles reporter Tim McManus, Cowboys reporter Todd Archer and national NFL reporter Dan Graziano dive deep on two of four NFC contenders before their "Monday Night Football" matchup.

Where do things stand with Eagles' and Cowboys' head coaches?

Nick Sirianni has a 61-28 record since taking over as coach in Philadelphia, has led the team to five playoff appearances in as many seasons and has gotten to the Super Bowl twice, winning one of them. You'd think he'd have a good bit of equity built up. 

That's being tested in 2026 with the Eagles in a four-game skid, dropping their record to 5-9 over the past 14 games dating to last season. Sirianni's in-game decision-making has had a hand in the current losing streak, though a depleted roster hit by injury, retirement (Lane Johnson) and trade (Cam Jurgens) is the primary culprit. 

The offense is lost right now and has had its share of issues during his tenure. Sirianni is a former offensive coordinator but the Eagles have outsourced a good chunk of those responsibilities, with mixed results. articles.headline: Mbappé double gives Madrid Clasico win over Barcelona
articles.description: Real Madrid cut the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to three points after Kylian Mbappé struck a late winner in a 2-1 win at the Nou Camp on Sunday.
articles.body:
Real Madrid cut the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to three points after Kylian Mbappé struck a late winner in a 2-1 win at the Nou Camp on Sunday.

Jose Mourinho's side looked set to miss the chance to put pressure on Hansi Flick's champions when Raphinha levelled the game at 1-1 just past the hour.

Mbappé's goal in the first half had Barça facing their first defeat of the season, but with the match heading for a draw the visitors hit them again in the 87th minute.

The winner was made by Jude Bellingham, showing good skill to release Eduardo Camavinga who cut back for the France international to fire in.

The champions had won all nine league matches so far this season and were looking to preserve their six-point advantage over Madrid, who despite the win stayed third.

Barça's lead at the top stayed at two points from Atletico Madrid as the title race was left looking far tighter than it might have after such an electric start to the campaign from Flick's side.

articles.headline: Sixers overrule Embiid, sit center with plantar fasciitis management
articles.description: Despite publicly calling to play Sunday against the Pistons, the 76ers decided to sit Joel Embiid due to right foot plantar fasciitis management.
articles.headlineJa: シックスターズ、エンビードの意向を覆し、足底筋膜炎のケアのためセンターを欠場させる
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のピストンズ戦への出場を公言していたものの、76ersは右足の足底筋膜炎のケアのため、ジョエル・エンビードを欠場させることを決定した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- A day after Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid asked reporters to campaign for him to play in Sunday's game against Detroit -- the second of the Sixers' first back-to-back this season -- the 76ers ruled out Embiid for Sunday night's game against the Detroit Pistons with right foot plantar fasciitis management. ​

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them," Embiid said with a smile after Saturday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

 

The Sixers decided against Embiid's wishes, as they look to keep the former MVP healthy for a long season. Embiid, plagued by various injuries, has averaged just 49 games per season over his 10 years.

In their win over the Bucks on Saturday, Embiid had his tenth career triple-double, finishing with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Having him sidelined is a significant blow to the Sixers' already thin frontcourt.

Philadelphia also ruled out big men Dominick Barlow (back), Jabari Walker (knee) and Tacko Fall (quad). Walker injured his left knee in Saturday's win, exiting the game in the third quarter. That leaves Adem Bona as the team's only true center active on Sunday. Forward Dean Wade, who made his season debut on Saturday, will likely play some center, and LeBron James, who missed Saturday's game with sciatica management, has no injury designation and can also help out at the center spot.

The Pistons will be without All-NBA center Jalen Duren, who the team said has a hamstring injury and will be out for at least two weeks.

articles.headline: McKennie scores 1st goal since April in much-needed Juventus win
articles.description: Weston McKennie opened the scoring for Juventus in a 2-0 win over Lecce on Sunday to help the Serie A side course correct after a pair of disappointing results.
articles.headlineJa: マッケニーが4月以来のゴールを決め、ユヴェントスが待望の勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ウェストン・マッケニーが日曜日のレッチェ戦で先制点を挙げ、ユヴェントスは2-0で勝利。2試合連続の不振に喘いでいたセリエAのチームにとって、軌道修正につながる重要な勝利となった。
articles.body:
Weston McKennie opened the scoring for Juventus in a 2-0 win over Lecce on Sunday to help the Serie A side course correct after a pair of disappointing results.

The United States midfielder swooped in to redirect a free kick over the top of the Lecce defense into the back of the net just before the 30-minute mark. It was his first goal in Serie A this season and first in all competitions for Juventus since April -- ending a 13-game drought.

Douglas Luiz scored another for the visitors just before halftime to Luciano Spalletti's side all it would need to pick up the three points and move up to seventh in the table on 14 points.

Juventus had lost their last game in Serie A -- a lackluster draw against Lazio last weekend -- before having to come from behind to draw with Stade Rennais 2-2 in the Europa League on Thursday.

Boos could be heard ringing down on Spalletti and his team after the draw with Rennes at the Allianz in Turin in midweek as the former Italy manager looks to get Juventus back on course in Serie A and in Europe.

McKennie was left out of the U.S. squad in the September/October international window in which Mauricio Pochettino brought in a number of new faces in the team's first games since losing to Belgium in the round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup last summer.

Information from ESPN Global Research was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Luis Enrique: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will be back stronger for PSG after ACL injury
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique says winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will come back stronger after he suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury.
articles.headlineJa: ルイス・エンリケ監督「クヴァラツヘリアはACL負傷から、より強くなってPSGに戻ってくる」
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンのルイス・エンリケ監督は、前十字靭帯（ACL）を負傷したウィングのフイチア・クヴァラツヘリアが、より強くなって復帰すると語った。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique says winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will come back stronger after he suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

The 25-year-old suffered the injury during PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona and is now ruled out for the remainder of the season.

Kvaratskhelia has been a key player for PSG over the last few years, having helped the club to back-to-back Champions League titles, and will be a big miss for Les Parisiens going forward.

Enrique says the Georgia international will continue to be an important player for the club once he has recovered from the injury.

He said: "Unfortunately, we already suspected after the game how serious the injury was. Our thoughts are with the player and what he's going to go through, it's difficult.

"But ultimately, you have to stay positive and remember that if you want to play at the highest level for 10 to 15 years, you're going to suffer injuries, that's the life of a professional footballer.

"Kvara is a fighter, you have to try and look for the positives, and there will be some, once he's overcome this injury. He has been, is and will continue to be a very important player for us. We'll stand by him and be attentive to his needs. He'll come back even stronger, I have no doubt about that.

"No injury means that we absolutely must sign a new player. Since the start of the season, I've always said that we could cope with any injuries."

PSG will welcome Lyon to Parc des Princes on Monday as they look for a fifth straight win, hoping to climb further up the table.

PSG were beaten 2-1 by Lyon in April in the last meeting between the two sides and Enrique says the result has given him extra motivation.

- PSG-Lyon match moved to Monday amid Paris protests, NFL game

- PSG star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptures ACL; Dembélé, Marquinhos out 'weeks'

- Cristiano Ronaldo leads Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tributes after ACL injury

He added: "It's a motivation to take on Paulo Fonseca's Olympique Lyonnais. We remember what they did last season, when they won at the Parc des Princes playing very well.

"It's up to us to show that we're ready for every game and to demonstrate our form. It's an extra motivation to play against this Olympique Lyonnais side.

"We've shown we can improve our results in the league. Three or four weeks ago, we were still a long way behind the top team in the table. And now, we have the chance to go top. It's important for us to be as high up the table as possible."

articles.headline: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois out of Clasico with flu
articles.description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss the team's Clásico clash with Barcelona with flu.
articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードのGKティボ・クルトワ、インフルエンザのためクラシコを欠場
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードのゴールキーパー、ティボ・クルトワは、インフルエンザによりバルセロナとのクラシコを欠場する。
articles.body:
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss the team's Clásico clash with Barcelona with flu.

Courtois, 34, is a key player for Madrid, but is absent for the LaLiga match at Camp Nou, which kicks off with Madrid trailing leaders Barça by six points in the table.

He is replaced in goal by Andriy Lunin, 27, who has been a regular deputy for Courtois in recent seasons, including in Madrid's run to the Champions League final in 2024.

"Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight's LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu," the club said in a brief statement before confirming his absence in their team announcement. "Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place."

Madrid go into the Clásico under pressure, having already lost twice in LaLiga this season -- at Real Betis and Atletico Madrid -- while Barcelona have won all of their league games.

However, Madrid's form has improved since the international break, with Courtois playing a starring role, including in their 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig in midweek.

The visitors will also be without Vinícius Júnior at Camp Nou, as he continues his four-game domestic ban.

articles.headline: Sunday's fantasy basketball adds and bets to make in the NBA
articles.description: Jim McCormick breaks down Sunday's slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Sunday

A seven-game Sunday slate features a series of potential competitive contests. Only one game on the docket claims a double-digit point spread -- a departure from a Saturday field that was full of large lines. The marquee matchup of the day features the Minnesota Timberwolves hosting the Toronto Raptors in a meeting of deep, darkhorse contenders.

Close games bode well for developing fantasy and betting angles, as rotations and workloads prove more predictable in competitive games. A good place to start during a busy day of basketball is the injury report, which tells us that we won't see Paolo Banchero, Zach Edey or Jalen Duren playing for their respective teams. Joel Embiid, meanwhile, is set to rest for the second leg of a back-to-back series for the Philadelphia 76ers.

While we're still learning how each rotation and coaching staff will react to the absence of big names from the gameplan, we can proactively make some decisions based on precedent and prediction. 

For the Orlando Magic, a proven veteran big man is due for more minutes and work in the wake of Banchero's ankle injury, as you'll read below. What will Memphis do sans Edey? How will Detroit cope with being sans their interior anchor in South Philly tonight? 

And, those 76ers don't have a one-to-one backup for Embiid like they did in seasons past in the form of Andre Drummond. They will instead likely turn to a collective and small-ball looks -- possible even some featuring LeBron at center. We'll learn a lot today about all of these sides, which can serve us in future slates, as well.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding

 Wendell Carter Jr., C, Orlando Magic (rostered in 23.5% of ESPN leagues)

With Banchero in street clothes for tonight's tilt with the New York Knicks, Carter should see more minutes, rebounding chances, and post touches as a result. The Knicks lack the interior defense and rebounding from last season's run, supporting confidence in double-double upside for this veteran big.

Paul Reed, C/PF, Detroit Pistons (14.2%)

Assuming Philadelphia decides to rest Embiid in the second game of a back-to-back, they will likely turn to a number of different looks to cover for him. Reed, who will consume a good bit of the work reserved for Duren, would then be facing a 76ers lineup badly lack rebounding acumen, establishing a nice floor for this active and unique frontcourt talent. It also helps that there is a fun narrative in play, as "B-ball Paul" began his career in Philly.

articles.headline: Pistons C Jalen Duren out at least two weeks with hamstring strain
articles.description: Pistons center Jalen Duren, who signed a five-year extension earlier this month, will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday.

Duren suffered the injury in the first half of Friday's win over the Miami Heat. He played only 10 minutes before leaving the game.

"It's tough when you lose a guy that means as much to us as JD does," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before Sunday's game in Philadelphia. "It's tough. Tough for him. Trying to come back and get himself situated to start the year. You miss those days. It's obviously a little bit difficult for us."

Duren's offseason was marked by a lengthy standoff with the Pistons over a contract extension. He missed media day and the first few practices of training camp before ultimately signing a five-year, $200 million deal.

Last season, he averaged a career high in points (19.5 PPG), made his first All-Star team and was named to the All-NBA third team as the Pistons earned the top seed in the Eastern Conference. But he struggled mightily in the postseason, dropping to 10.2 points per game in 14 playoff games before Detroit's second-round exit.

Duren scored 22 points with nine rebounds in Detroit's season-opening win over the Boston Celtics.

Information from The Associated Press and ESPN's Jamal Collier was used in this report.
